front: In a survey of 80 admissions at one hospital, what is the statistical unit?
back: An admission. The unit is the entity on which the variable is recorded. Define admissions versus distinct patients carefully.

front: Which variable is nominal?
back: Blood group. Blood-group categories have no intrinsic ordering.

front: Why is an average of ward codes 1, 2 and 3 usually meaningless?
back: The codes are arbitrary labels. The numbers label nominal categories and do not quantify distances.

front: A binary indicator is 1 for 18 of 30 patients. Its mean is…
back: 0.60. The mean of 0/1 values equals the fraction of ones: 18/30.

front: Stays are 2, 3, 3, 4 and 8 days. What is the median?
back: 3 days. The ordered sample has five observations; the third is 3.

front: For any numeric sample, Σ(xᵢ−x̄) equals…
back: 0. The mean balances the positive and negative deviations.

front: For values 2 and 3, Σxᵢ² equals…
back: 13. Square each value before summing: 4+9. Squaring the sum gives 25.

front: Which pair of Excel functions uses denominator n−1?
back: VAR.S and STDEV.S. The .S functions return adjusted sample variance and SD.

front: For values 2, 4 and 6, the descriptive variance with denominator n is…
back: 8/3. The mean is 4, so the squared deviations sum to 8; divide by 3.

front: Q1=10 and Q3=18. Which observation is beyond the upper 1.5 IQR fence?
back: 31. IQR=8 and the upper fence is 18+12=30. A value strictly greater than 30 is flagged.

front: In simple random sampling without replacement, which statement defines the design?
back: Every subset of the specified size is equally likely. Equal probability applies to each possible size-n sample, not merely to convenient units.

front: A stratified sample differs from a cluster sample because it…
back: Samples within every stratum. A basic stratified design samples within every stratum; a cluster design selects clusters.

front: Every 10th record is selected after a random start. This is…
back: Systematic sampling. Systematic sampling has a random start and a regular interval, but not all subsets are possible.

front: A very large volunteer survey can still have…
back: Selection bias. Large n reduces random error, not systematic self-selection.

front: Which is a valid discrete probability distribution?
back: 0.2, 0.5, 0.3. Probabilities must be nonnegative and sum to 1.

front: X takes 0, 1, 2 with probabilities 0.2, 0.5, 0.3. E(X) is…
For Bernoulli X with π=0.25, Var(X) is…
back: 0.1875. Bernoulli variance is π(1−π)=0.25×0.75.

front: For a continuous model, P(X=exactly a) is…
back: 0. A single point has zero area in a continuous distribution.

front: A probability density may exceed 1 because…
back: Probability is area, rather than curve height. A sufficiently narrow density can exceed 1 while its total area is 1.

front: The CDF F(a) represents…
back: P(X≤a). The cumulative distribution accumulates probability to the left.

front: Which is an estimand in a hospital waiting-time study?
back: The unknown population mean waiting time. The estimand is the target parameter, rather than a rule or observed number.

front: The observed x̄=24.2 is an…
back: Estimate. An estimate is the realised number calculated from one sample.

front: The sampling distribution of X̄ describes…
back: Means across repeated same-size samples. It is a distribution of a statistic under repeated sampling.

front: For independent observations, E(X̄) equals…
back: μ. The sample mean is unbiased for the population mean.

front: Population SD is 12 and n=36. SE(X̄) is…
To halve SE while holding population SD fixed, sample size must be…
back: Quadrupled. SE scales as 1/√n.

front: Increasing sample size mechanically reduces…
back: The SE of the mean. Sample means become more precise; individual population variation does not vanish.

front: An unbiased estimator means…
back: Its repeated-sampling expectation equals the target. Unbiasedness concerns an average over the sampling distribution.

front: Which quantity is unbiased for population variance under independent sampling?
back: S² with denominator n−1. The adjusted variance corrects the downward bias caused by estimating the mean.

front: For an independent sample of size 5, E(Vₙ) with denominator n is…
A confidence interval is generally…
back: Estimate ± critical value × SE. A critical value converts standard error into a margin of error.

front: For x̄=80, known σ=12 and n=36, the 95% normal CI is approximately…
A 90% two-sided normal CI uses z≈…
back: 1.645. The cumulative probability for the upper critical value is 0.95.

front: For unknown population variance and normal sampling, the mean interval uses…
back: s and t with n−1 df. Estimate the SD with STDEV.S and account for its uncertainty with t.

front: For n=16, the two-sided t interval uses…
back: 15 df. One mean has been estimated, giving n−1 degrees of freedom.

front: A higher confidence level with the same data produces…
back: A wider interval. It changes the critical value, not the data-based SE.

front: At fixed SD and critical value, quadrupling n changes interval width to…
back: Half. Width scales with SE and hence 1/√n.

front: The 95% confidence level refers to…
back: Coverage of repeated intervals from the procedure. Before sampling, endpoints vary. Approximately 95% of valid repeated intervals contain fixed μ.

front: For a mean interval, the full width equals…
back: Twice the margin of error. Width is U−L=2×critical×SE.

front: 120 successes among 200 observations gives p̂=…
back: 0.60. The sample proportion is successes divided by total n.

front: Which correctly states a two-sided mean test?
back: H₀:μ=100; Hₐ:μ≠100. Hypotheses concern the unknown population parameter.

front: Known σ=10, n=100, x̄=103 and μ₀=100. The z statistic is…
Unknown σ, n=16, x̄=12, s=4 and μ₀=10. The t statistic is…
back: 2 with 15 df. SE=4/4=1 and t=2/1=2; df=15.

front: A two-sided test compares the observed statistic using…
back: Its absolute magnitude. Both sufficiently positive and negative values can reject a two-sided null.

front: For p=0.032 at α=0.05, the decision is…
back: Reject H₀. 0.032<0.05. The sign affects interpretation, not this two-sided rule.

front: For p=0.12 at α=0.05, a defensible conclusion is…
back: Insufficient evidence to reject H₀. Failure to reject is not proof of equality.

front: The p-value is conditional on…
back: H₀ and the sampling model. It measures extreme-statistic probability under the null assumptions.

front: A Type I error means…
back: Rejecting a true H₀. α controls the Type I error probability under the model.

front: Statistical power is…
back: 1−β. β is the probability of failing to reject a false null at a specified alternative. Supplementary context beyond the supplied Topic 5 slide deck.

front: A proportion test under H₀:π=0.50 uses which SE?
back: √[0.50×0.50/n]. The null reference variance uses the null parameter π₀.

front: Which comparison is paired?
back: The same patients measured before and after treatment. Pairing comes from matching observations, not equal sample sizes.

front: For independent groups, SE of the difference is…
back: √(s₁²/n₁+s₂²/n₂). Each independent mean contributes its variance; add these variances and take the square root.

front: If x̄₁=125 and x̄₂=129, x̄₁−x̄₂ is…
back: −4. Subtract in the defined group order, retaining the outcome units.

front: Reversing group order changes a two-sided test by…
back: Reversing the statistic’s sign but keeping its p-value. The magnitude and uncertainty of the contrast are unchanged.

front: The course’s main Topic 6 calculation uses…
back: A large-sample normal approximation for independent means. The supplied slides use large independent samples and approximate t by z.

front: A 95% CI for μ₁−μ₂ entirely below zero indicates…
back: An estimated lower population mean in group 1. The sign concerns the mean contrast; causal interpretation needs study-design support.

front: For a paired mean test, s_d is…
back: Adjusted SD of the individual paired differences. Compute each dᵢ first, then its adjusted SD.

front: The pooled equal-variance two-mean test assumes…
back: Equal population variances. Pooling is justified by a common-variance assumption.

front: For the pooled t test with n₁=20 and n₂=25, df is…
back: 43. df=n₁+n₂−2=43, under the equal-variance normal model.

front: A significance-star legend should be…
back: Read for that specific paper. Authors use different star thresholds and footnotes.
